evidence: Plin. NH 20.175: orīganum … plūra genera in medicīnā habet
terms.comment: Greek ὀρίγανον; Lewis & Short: “wild marjoram, origan”, also orīganus m. Pliny says it has several kinds (NH 20.175–177). Botanists keep the word for the genus Origanum, which takes in marjoram too, but Latin, like English, has another word for marjoram (see marjoram).

phrases.latin: Orīganum, quod vī sapōrem cunīlae aemulātur, ut dīximus, plūra genera in medicīnā habet.
phrases.english: Oregano, which in strength rivals the taste of cunila, as we have said, has several kinds in medicine.

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. oregano.
